findings.description: The explicit human request to remove the flowing dots was not followed. All 28 independent physical links still animate, with one moving dot per route in five 100ms samples. One dot is not zero. The source-backed animation setting is off; this is an instruction/meaning-ledger failure, not missing motion evidence.

Fourteen visible text runs retain uncertain individual edge ownership: v1=3, v2=3, v3=6, v4=2. The fused v4 run contains two labels with no separator, so this is 15 label units. These are not missing endpoints or cross-view relation loss: all 28 routes remain traceable. They fail the per-link label-meaning/readability gate; the clearest contradictory proximity is active immediately beside the dashed standby stem at v2 [31,14,6,1]. Edge ids list affected or competing nearby links, not an inferred unique ownership assignment. Homogeneous ECMP/x-connect text makes the broad tier meaning recoverable but does not establish individual label owners.

At v4 [33,22,8,1], two required dual labels touch as dualdual, one uninterrupted RGB (235,219,178) run. The two substrings at [33,22,4,1] and [37,22,4,1] have no visible separator. This breaks both label ownership (F02) and full-label layout readability even though all characters and boxes fit inside 77x47. It is not clipping and not a missing route.

Only four final-pane manifests retain confirmed_closed results. generation.json claims seven owned/closed panes but says discarded probe capture directories were removed. The supplied case tree has no preserved capture/cleanup probe for w7E:p76, w7E:p78, or w7E:p79, so cleanup including failures/superseded captures is not independently verifiable. This blocks workflow_evidence and cleanup verification; it does not assert that those panes leaked. No pixel coordinate is applicable to a missing execution record.
